_transcription: ENGLISH half only, CBSE Class 10 Mathematics Standard (041), Series WX1YZ/2, Set 2. 23 pages (idx 0-22): idx 0 cover, idx 1 Hindi instructions, English on every even index 2-22, Hindi on every odd index (each the Hindi of the page after it). Every odd-page top checked on the contact sheet: all open with a Hindi block, none carries English spill-over; last page idx 22 is English. Instruction (viii) prints 2 internal choices in B, 2 in C, 2 in D and 3 in E: Q21, Q23, Q27, Q28, Q33, Q35, Q36 (ii), Q37 (iii), Q38 (ii), all found on the paper and each confirmed by a bare OR in the marking scheme for 30/2/2. Section-A keys read off the marking scheme for 30/2/2 and each re-derived: all agree; no voids. Decimal points are RAISED (Q5 0·3, Q31 3·14, Q35 1·73). Sibling of 30/2/1: 41 of 53 rows are the same questions, reshuffled and renumbered, and reuse 30/2/1's text byte for byte; 12 rows are new (Q1, Q2, Q5, Q11, Q12, Q20, Q25, Q26, Q31, Q34, Q35a, Q35b). The case studies are reordered: CBL is Case Study 1 here (Case Study 3 in 30/2/1), the memento Case Study 2 (1), the coffee cups Case Study 3 (2).

questions.subtopic: Geometrical Meaning of the Zeroes of a Polynomial
questions.context: Questions number 19 and 20 are Assertion and Reason based questions carrying 1 mark each. Two statements are given, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (a), (b), (c) and (d) as given below.
questions.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** The polynomial \(p(x) = x^2 + 3x + 3\) has two real zeroes.

**Reason (R) :** A quadratic polynomial can have at most two real zeroes.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

| Number of Computers | Number of Schools |
|---|---|
| 1 – 10 | 250 |
| 11 – 20 | 200 |
| 21 – 50 | 290 |
| 51 – 100 | 180 |
| 101 and more | 80 |

One school is chosen at random. Then :
questions.stem: Find the probability that the school chosen at random has more than 100 computers.
